scope: All particles predicted. No MPM or force network at inference. Reference data use dynamic two-way MJWarp–MPM.

results.name: Diverse reference data collected
results.summary: 66 complete dynamic episodes: 48 training, 6 validation, 12 reserved test. Each has 300 steps at 5 ms and 4,000 particles. Shapes: box, sphere, cylinder. Training density 800–2400 kg/m³; material friction 0.25–0.70; Young modulus 10^5–10^15 Pa; moving-body mass 1–4 kg. Validation/test use separate parameter combinations.

results.name: Initial GNN: insufficient rollout stability
results.summary: A 64-channel, three-pass graph network trained for 5,000 updates. Its selected validation checkpoint slightly improves one-step velocity prediction over keeping the current velocity. Full rollouts show large particle drift and inaccurate body forces.

limitations: This is a failed initial baseline, not a validated replacement for MPM.
Validation is used for development; reserved test episodes have not been evaluated.
The current coupled diagnostic uses free-body integration and stops if the body intersects the rigid tray.
Material stress, plastic strain, and MPM grid state are not network inputs. Velocity history may not fully describe material memory.
Sampled SDF support is implemented; rollout accuracy and cost still need measurement.
These are 0.32 m × 0.32 m × 0.16 m material beds. Large G1 testbed scaling remains untested for the GNN.
